read_h04_csv <- function(relative_path) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(root, relative_path), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

h04_gt <- function(table, font_size = 12) {
  table |>
    gt::opt_row_striping() |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      table.font.size = gt::px(font_size),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(4),
      column_labels.font.weight = "600",
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11)
    )
}

format_p <- function(value, significant = FALSE) {
  displayed <- ifelse(
    is.na(value),
    "—",
    ifelse(value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", value))
  )
  ifelse(significant & !is.na(value), paste0("**", displayed, "**"), displayed)
}

## About this analysis record

::: {.callout-note title="About this analysis record"}
This page explains how verified one-hour melEDI records and multi-select
self-reported activity reports were turned into the scientific results. The
[H04 results report](../../../notebooks/hypotheses/H04.qmd) presents the
findings and its [preregistration changes](../../../notebooks/hypotheses/H04.qmd#h04-preregistration-deviations).
:::

H04 asks whether hourly self-reported activity categories are associated with
hourly geometric mean melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI), a
melanopsin-weighted measure of illuminance expressed in lux. The primary
near-eye sensor position measures light near the eyes but is not a retinal
measurement. The complementary chest sensor position is not a measure of
ocular exposure. The five interpretable categories are At home, Office/home
working, Outdoors, Vehicle/public transport, and Sleeping. Other/unspecified
activity remains in the additive population-mean model as a display-only row,
is a varied display-only category rather than a coherent scientific category,
and supports no substantive claim.

Activity categories are not mutually exclusive behavioural states. When an
hour contains several retained labels, that hour contributes $1/k$ to each of
its $k$ labels. The central category estimand is therefore average melEDI
associated with each reported collapsed activity category, with the hour's
contribution shared across concurrent reports. It is not a causal effect.

A participant-hour is one original hourly record for one participant; the
concurrent selections share that one hour rather than creating independent
duplicates. A participant-day groups that participant's records within one
study day.

A site-average estimate is an average across the observed study sites that
gives each site equal weight. The activity-by-site interaction model allows
the association between activity category and melEDI to differ by study site.

This page identifies the data and code that produced the result, explains why
each operation was needed, and shows the recorded evidence used to check it.
Shared coverage and model-ready dataset definitions are documented in
[Preparation 02](../../../notebooks/preparation/02_coverage_sample_flow.qmd)
and [Preparation 06](../../../notebooks/preparation/06_model_ready_datasets.qmd).

## Verified inputs and activity representation

### File identity

Five files determine the scientific H04 frames and displays: the normalized
activity diary, the primary near-eye and complementary chest one-hour
outcomes, the gap-timing-unaware one-hour outcomes, and the shared
country-coded site registry. Their complete SHA-256 identities and current
contract identities are recorded. The recorded R 4.6.1 comparison establishes
zero-tolerance equality of all values in all 14 H04 analysis frames, so the
accepted model objects and results remain controlling and no model refit is
required.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-input-identities
#| tbl-cap: "Verified inputs used by the H04 result-producing analysis."

result_input_ids <- c(
  "normalized_diary",
  "main_near_eye",
  "main_chest",
  "gap_timing_unaware",
  "site_registry"
)
input_labels <- c(
  normalized_diary = "Normalized activity diary",
  main_near_eye = "Primary near-eye one-hour outcome",
  main_chest = "Complementary chest one-hour outcome",
  gap_timing_unaware = "Gap-timing-unaware one-hour outcomes",
  site_registry = "Shared country-coded site registry"
)

verified_inputs <- input_audit |>
  filter(.data$input_id %in% result_input_ids) |>
  left_join(
    input_reconciliation |>
      select(
        "input_id",
        "current_contract_sha256",
        "current_contract_verified",
        "all_downstream_frame_values_identical"
      ),
    by = "input_id",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    current_sha256 = vapply(.data$path, artifact_sha256, character(1)),
    Input = unname(input_labels[.data$input_id]),
    Path = if_else(
      startsWith(.data$path, paste0(root, "/")),
      substring(.data$path, nchar(root) + 2L),
      basename(.data$path)
    ),
    `Accepted SHA-256 prefix` = substr(.data$sha256, 1L, 12L),
    `Current SHA-256 prefix` = substr(.data$current_sha256, 1L, 12L),
    verification_state = case_when(
      .data$current_sha256 == .data$sha256 ~ "PASS",
      .data$current_contract_verified &
        .data$all_downstream_frame_values_identical ~ "VERIFIED CURRENT IDENTITY",
      TRUE ~ "FAIL"
    )
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(verified_inputs) == 5L,
  all(
    verified_inputs$verification_state %in%
      c("PASS", "VERIFIED CURRENT IDENTITY")
  )
)

verified_inputs |>
  mutate(
    Verification = recode(
      .data$verification_state,
      PASS = "Verified",
      `VERIFIED CURRENT IDENTITY` = "Verified current identity",
      FAIL = "Review needed"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    "Input",
    "Path",
    "Accepted SHA-256 prefix",
    "Current SHA-256 prefix",
    "Verification"
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Input ~ gt::pct(22),
    Path ~ gt::pct(39),
    `Accepted SHA-256 prefix` ~ gt::pct(13),
    `Current SHA-256 prefix` ~ gt::pct(13),
    Verification ~ gt::pct(13)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    paste(
      "Complete accepted identities are retained in H04_input_audit.csv;",
      "the current contract identities and exact frame-value comparison",
      "are retained in H04_metric010_input_reconciliation.csv and",
      "H04_metric010_frame_invariance.csv."
    )
  ) |>
  h04_gt(11)
```

### Activity transformation

The diary transformation is outcome-blind. It first combines the three
outdoor flags, travel by bicycle/on foot, working outdoors, and free time
outdoors, into **Outdoors**. It then deduplicates collapsed labels within an
hour. If Other is selected with a named category, only the named category or
categories are retained; Other is retained only when it is the sole selected
label. Free text is neither inspected nor recoded.

After these operations, the retained distinct labels are pivoted to long
format. If hour $h$ contains $k_h$ labels, each long row receives

$$
w_{hc}=\frac{1}{k_h}, \qquad \sum_{c=1}^{k_h} w_{hc}=1.
$$

Thus an original hour contributes one total unit, whether it supplies one,
two, or three activity memberships. Using unweighted long rows would instead
estimate a selection-level association in which multi-select hours count more
than single-select hours.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-transformation
#| tbl-cap: "Implemented multi-select activity transformation."

tibble::tribble(
  ~Order, ~Operation, ~Scientific_reason,
  1L, "Collapse three outdoor flags before pivoting", "Represents outdoor mobility, outdoor work, and outdoor free time with the reader-facing category Outdoors.",
  2L, "Deduplicate collapsed labels within participant-hour", "Prevents two source flags that collapse to the same label from creating duplicate analytical memberships.",
  3L, "Apply the Other specificity rule", "Retains named information when present and keeps Other only as a varied display-only Other-only category, not a coherent scientific category.",
  4L, "Pivot one row per retained distinct label", "Preserves simultaneous reports without declaring them independent behavioural states.",
  5L, "Assign analysis weight 1/k", "Makes the total contribution of every original participant-hour equal to one.",
  6L, "Cluster inference by participant", "Encompasses concurrent within-hour memberships and the longitudinal record within the same covariance cluster."
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Order) |>
  gt::cols_label(Scientific_reason = "Scientific reason") |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Order ~ gt::pct(6),
    Operation ~ gt::pct(34),
    Scientific_reason ~ gt::pct(60)
  ) |>
  h04_gt(10.8)
```

## Model frames, outcome, and support

### Sample flow

Hours with no retained category are not interpreted as “no activity.” They
remain outside the category model and are counted separately below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-sample-flow
#| tbl-cap: "Exact one-hour sample flow into the primary H04 model frames."

sample_flow |>
  filter(!is.na(.data$outcome_grid_hours)) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Outcome grid hours` = .data$outcome_grid_hours,
    `Outcome unavailable` = .data$outcome_unavailable_hours,
    `No eligible diary key` =
      .data$outcome_hours_without_eligible_diary_key,
    `No retained activity category` =
      .data$outcome_hours_with_no_retained_activity,
    `Fitted unique hours` = .data$model_candidate_unique_hours,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Sites = .data$sites,
    `Generated long rows` = .data$generated_long_rows,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric), sep_mark = ",") |>
  h04_gt(10)
```

The primary near-eye frame contains 16,526 unique participant-hours, 17,266
long rows, 126 participants, 724 participant-days, and nine sites. The chest
frame contains 20,128 unique participant-hours, 21,071 long rows, 150
participants, 875 participant-days, and eight sites. The effective weighted
hours equal the unique hours exactly.

### Outcome definition and exact zeros

The response is the exact one-hour zero-aware geometric mean melEDI in lux,
calculated from at least 30 valid minutes. No logarithmic offset is added to
the primary response. Exact zero remains in every fitted mean model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-zero-support
#| tbl-cap: "Exact-zero and positive melEDI support in the primary frames."

zero_summary |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Unique participant-hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Exact-zero hours` = .data$exact_zero_unique_hours,
    `Exact-zero fraction` = .data$exact_zero_fraction,
    `Positive median (lx)` = .data$positive_median_lx,
    `Positive 95th percentile (lx)` =
      .data$positive_95th_percentile_lx,
    `Maximum (lx)` = .data$maximum_lx,
    `Zeros retained` = if_else(
      .data$zeros_retained_in_models,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    )
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(`Unique participant-hours`, `Exact-zero hours`),
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = `Exact-zero fraction`, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Positive median (lx)`,
      `Positive 95th percentile (lx)`,
      `Maximum (lx)`
    ),
    decimals = 1,
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  h04_gt(11)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h04-prep-positive-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of positive one-hour geometric melEDI in the primary model frames. Each long row contributes its accepted 1/k weight, so every original participant-hour contributes one total unit to one response bin. Exact-zero hours are reported separately above and remained in the fitted models."
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked histograms show the effective weighted hours across positive one-hour melEDI values for the primary near-eye and complementary chest sensor positions. Both distributions are strongly right-skewed, extend from below 0.001 lux to tens of thousands of lux, and contain most positive weighted hours between about 1 and 1,000 lux. Exact zeros are not drawn in this positive-only histogram."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.8

ggplot(
  response_distribution |>
    mutate(
      placement = factor(
        .data$placement,
        levels = c("Near-eye", "Chest")
      )
    ),
  aes(
    x = .data$log10_midpoint,
    y = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    fill = .data$placement
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.235, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(vars(.data$placement), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = placement_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-4, -2, 0, 2, 4),
    labels = c("0.0001", "0.01", "1", "100", "10,000"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ","),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Positive one-hour geometric melEDI (lx; log10-spaced bins)",
    y = "Effective weighted participant-hours"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )
```

The exact weighted bin values are available as [figure source
data](../../../artifacts/11_source_data/H04/H04_preparation_positive_response_distribution.csv).

### Recorded-frame integrity

The recorded primary long frames contain one row for each distinct retained
hour/activity membership. A repeated outcome is therefore intentional when an
hour has several labels; it is not a repeated independent observation. The
integrity checks group those rows back to their original hour and verify the
response, participant, participant-day, $k$, and total weight.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-integrity
#| tbl-cap: "Bounded integrity checks of the recorded primary H04 model frames."

integrity_display <- frame_integrity |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Unique participant-hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Long rows` = .data$long_rows,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    `Duplicate hour/activity rows` =
      .data$duplicate_hour_activity_memberships,
    `Response conflicts within hour` = .data$hour_response_conflicts,
    `Rows unequal to k` = .data$row_k_mismatches,
    `Maximum |sum(weight) − 1|` = .data$maximum_weight_sum_error,
    `Co-selected Other rows retained` =
      .data$co_selected_other_retained_rows,
    `Invalid outcome or weight rows` =
      .data$invalid_response_rows + .data$invalid_weight_rows
  )
stopifnot(

  all(integrity_display$`Response conflicts within hour` == 0L),
  all(integrity_display$`Rows unequal to k` == 0L),

)

integrity_display |>

  h04_gt(10.5)
```

## Population-mean and activity-by-site models

### Additive population-mean model

The primary question is tested with the exact Wilkinson formula:

```r
geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity
```

`geo_medi_1h` is the one-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI in lux. The model
uses a log link and the quasi-Tweedie working variance
$\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X)=\phi\mu^{1.539919}$. Site is a fixed factor with
sum contrasts; activity is a fixed six-level factor with At home as the
treatment reference. Each long row receives its exact `analysis_weight = 1/k`.

Repeated memberships and longitudinal observations are addressed for
inference with participant-clustered HC1 sandwich covariance. Denominator
degrees of freedom equal the number of participant clusters minus one, and
reported intervals are two-sided 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). This
participant-cluster-robust construction allows observations from the same
participant to be related. The formula contains no random effect.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-primary-specification
#| tbl-cap: "Primary and complementary population-mean model settings."

tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Near_eye, ~Chest,
  "Formula", "geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity", "geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity",
  "Response", "One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx)", "One-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI (lx)",
  "Mean and variance", "Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919", "Log link; quasi-Tweedie p = 1.539919",
  "Long-row weight", "1/k retained labels in the original hour", "1/k retained labels in the original hour",
  "Activity reference", "At home", "At home",
  "Site", "Nine-level fixed factor; sum contrasts", "Eight-level fixed factor; sum contrasts",
  "Uncertainty", "Participant-clustered HC1; df = 125", "Participant-clustered HC1; df = 149",
  "Reported named-category mean", "Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model", "Site-average estimate from the supported interaction model",
  "Role", "Primary inference", "Complementary evidence"
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(Near_eye = "Near eye", Chest = "Chest") |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Component ~ gt::pct(21),
    Near_eye ~ gt::pct(39.5),
    Chest ~ gt::pct(39.5)
  ) |>
  h04_gt(11)
```

Cluster-robust covariance protects coefficient uncertainty against
unspecified within-participant dependence under its large-cluster assumptions.
It does not remove serial structure from residuals or make the working
Tweedie distribution a calibrated model of the exact-zero process.

### Exact formulas and robust restrictions

The comparison formulas below are recorded for construction and rank checks.
The category decisions use robust Wald restrictions on the full fitted model;
they are not likelihood-ratio tests against the comparison formula.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-formulas
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded H04 formulas used for the population-mean, activity-by-site interaction, and temporal analyses."

formula_labels <- c(
  primary_full = "Primary additive mean model",
  secondary_mundlak_audit = "Mundlak within/between sensitivity",
  primary_five_named_null = "Five-named-category comparison formula; Other unrestricted",
  secondary_six_category_null = "Six-category comparison formula",
  heterogeneity_five_named_full = "Five-named-category activity-by-site interaction",
  heterogeneity_five_named_additive = "Five-named-category additive comparison",
  temporal_no_activity = "Exploratory temporal comparator",
  temporal_activity_long = "Exploratory temporal activity model"
)

formula_registry |>
  filter(.data$formula_id %in% names(formula_labels)) |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = unname(formula_labels[.data$formula_id]),
    Formula = .data$formula
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(Analysis ~ gt::pct(34), Formula ~ gt::pct(66)) |>
  h04_gt(10)
```

The primary restriction tests equality of the five named category means with
four independent rows while leaving the Other coefficient unrestricted. The
secondary restriction adds Other and tests equality of all six categories
with five rows.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-primary-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded additive-model category omnibus tests."

primary_tests |>
  filter(.data$decision_role %in% c("PRIMARY", "SECONDARY")) |>
  mutate(
    Test = recode(
      .data$decision_role,
      PRIMARY = "Five interpretable categories; Other unrestricted",
      SECONDARY = "All six categories"
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Test = .data$Test,
    Restrictions = .data$restrictions,
    `Participant clusters` = .data$clusters,
    `Denominator df` = .data$denominator_df,
    `Wald F` = .data$f_statistic,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$p_raw, .data$p_raw < 0.05),
    Status = recode(.data$status, ESTIMABLE = "Estimable")
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Wald F`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Raw p`) |>
  h04_gt(10.5)
```

The near-eye primary test is $F(4,125)=83.59$, raw $p<0.001$. The separate
chest result is $F(4,149)=93.31$, raw $p<0.001$.

### Estimands, references, and standardization

For a category and each site observed in a placement, a design row is
constructed on the fitted log-mean scale. Sites contribute equal weight, the
design rows are averaged, and one exponential back-transformation is applied,
returning the site-average estimate to melEDI in lux. This is a geometric
site-average expectation, not an arithmetic mean of response-scale site
predictions.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-estimand-contract
#| tbl-cap: "Reported H04 estimands and their reference distributions."

tibble::tribble(
  ~Estimand, ~Source_model, ~Reference_distribution, ~Inferential_role,
  "Primary category omnibus", "Additive site + activity model", "All retained fractionally weighted near-eye memberships", "Four-restriction robust equality test for the five interpretable categories",
  "Mundlak within-participant category contrast", "Additive site + activity model with participant-level category proportions", "Current activity category at the weighted mean participant composition", "Four named ratios to At home with participant-clustered 95% CIs and FDR",
  "Mundlak between-participant composition", "Same Mundlak sensitivity model", "10 percentage-point higher usual category share replacing At home", "Four named composition ratios with participant-clustered 95% CIs and FDR",
  "Named-category mean melEDI", "Supported five-category activity-by-site interaction model", "Site-average: observed sites weighted equally on the fitted log-mean scale", "Descriptive geometric expectation with 95% CI",
  "Other/unspecified mean melEDI", "Additive model", "Site-average: observed sites weighted equally on the fitted log-mean scale", "Display only; no substantive claim",
  "Named-category ratio", "Same model as the corresponding named-category mean", "At home with the same site-average weights", "Four non-reference ratios; FDR within sensor position",
  "Named-category difference", "Same model as the corresponding named-category mean", "At home with the same site-average weights", "Absolute magnitude summary with 95% CI",
  "Activity-by-site interaction omnibus", "Five-category activity-by-site interaction model", "All estimable named-category site departures", "One raw robust additivity test per sensor position",
  "Site deviation", "Five-category activity-by-site interaction model", "Site-specific category mean divided by its site-average category mean", "Supported cells only; FDR within sensor position"
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(
    Source_model = "Source model",
    Reference_distribution = "Reference distribution",
    Inferential_role = "Inferential role"
  ) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Estimand ~ gt::pct(20),
    Source_model ~ gt::pct(25),
    Reference_distribution ~ gt::pct(29),
    Inferential_role ~ gt::pct(26)
  ) |>
  h04_gt(10.2)
```

At home is the reader-facing and model reference. The four named-versus-home
ratios form one complete false-discovery-rate (FDR) family within each sensor
position. Other is not a member of that family.

### Activity-by-site interaction

The activity-by-site interaction is examined separately from the additive
primary omnibus with the five interpretable categories. It allows the
association between activity category and melEDI to differ by study site:

```r
geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named
```

Other-only hours are omitted from this model. The near-eye and chest designs
are full rank and do not force an Other interaction in a sparse site. Site
specific outputs are emitted only for cells that pass the reporting support
rule.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-heterogeneity-checks
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded estimability checks for the five-category activity-by-site interaction models."

heterogeneity_checks |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Formula = .data$formula,
    `Unique participant-hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Long rows` = .data$long_rows,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Full rank` = if_else(.data$full_rank, "Yes", "No"),
    Restrictions = .data$restriction_df,
    `Restriction covariance positive definite` = if_else(
      .data$restriction_covariance_positive_definite,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    ),
    `Maximum cluster score share` = .data$maximum_cluster_score_share,
    `Maximum cluster leverage share` =
      .data$maximum_cluster_leverage_share,
    `Construction result` = if_else(.data$gate_pass, "Supported", "Unsupported")
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(
      `Unique participant-hours`,
      `Long rows`,
      `Effective weighted hours`,
      Participants,
      Restrictions
    ),
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Maximum cluster score share`,
      `Maximum cluster leverage share`
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.4)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-heterogeneity-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded robust activity-by-site interaction tests for the five named categories."

primary_tests |>
  filter(nzchar(.data$selected_architecture)) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Restrictions = .data$restrictions,
    `Participant clusters` = .data$clusters,
    `Denominator df` = .data$denominator_df,
    `Wald F` = .data$f_statistic,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$p_raw, .data$p_raw < 0.05),
    Status = recode(.data$status, ESTIMABLE = "Estimable")
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Wald F`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Raw p`) |>
  h04_gt()
```

The supported activity-by-site interaction tests were $F(32,125)=8.03$ at the
near-eye sensor position and $F(28,149)=11.62$ at the chest sensor position,
both raw $p<0.001$. These results justify using the interaction models for the
descriptive named-category summaries. They do not support post-hoc site
ranking.

### Exploratory participant random-intercept decomposition {#sec-h04-prep-participant-random-intercept}

The population-mean quasi-Tweedie GLM and participant-clustered covariance
remain the inferential analysis. A separate mixed model describes
participant-level variation in the support-qualified five-category
activity-by-site frame. The random intercept lets participants have different
overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure:

```r
geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + (1 | participant)
```

The generalized linear mixed model was fitted in R with `glmmTMB`, using a
Tweedie distribution with a log link, maximum likelihood, and the
fixed working power 1.539919. The exact `analysis_weight = 1/k` enters every
fit. Other-only hours are absent because this branch inherits the supported
five-named-category interaction frame. The near-eye fit therefore uses 16,875
long rows representing 16,135 participant-hours from 126 participants. The
chest fit uses 20,440 long rows representing 19,497 participant-hours from 150
participants.

This descriptive mixed-model decomposition is distinct from the
population-mean Mundlak-style sensitivity, which adjusts current-category
contrasts for participants' usual activity composition. Neither assessment
changes the primary analysis or its multiplicity families.

The standard Nakagawa implementation calculates the fixed-predictor variance
with an unweighted variance across fitted rows. That convention would give a
multi-select hour more influence because it has more rows. The H04 calculation
instead uses the fractional-frequency sample variance

$$
\sigma_f^2 =
\frac{\sum_i w_i(\eta_i-\bar\eta_w)^2}{\sum_i w_i-1},
\qquad
\bar\eta_w = \frac{\sum_i w_i\eta_i}{\sum_i w_i},
$$

where $w_i=1/k$ and $\eta_i$ is the fixed-effects linear predictor. This
reduces exactly to the H03 convention when every hour has one row. The
participant-intercept variance $\sigma_u^2$ and the lognormal
distribution-specific variance $\sigma_e^2$ follow the same
`insight::get_variance()` convention. The reported values are

$$
R_m^2 = \frac{\sigma_f^2}{\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2+\sigma_e^2},
\qquad
R_c^2 = \frac{\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2}
{\sigma_f^2+\sigma_u^2+\sigma_e^2}.
$$

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-participant-r2
#| tbl-cap: "Stored fractionally weighted mixed-model R² and participant-intercept summaries."

participant_random_intercept |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Long rows` = .data$long_rows,
    `Unique participant-hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Marginal R²` = .data$marginal_r_squared,
    `Conditional R²` = .data$conditional_r_squared,
    `Participant increment` = .data$participant_r_squared_increment,
    `Distribution-specific remainder` = .data$residual_variance_share,
    `Adjusted participant ICC` = .data$adjusted_participant_icc,
    `One-SD participant factor` = .data$participant_factor_per_sd,
    `Unweighted-row marginal R²` =
      .data$conventional_unweighted_row_marginal_r_squared
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(`Long rows`, `Unique participant-hours`, Participants),
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = `Effective weighted hours`,
    decimals = 0,
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Marginal R²`,
      `Conditional R²`,
      `Participant increment`,
      `Distribution-specific remainder`,
      `Adjusted participant ICC`,
      `Unweighted-row marginal R²`
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `One-SD participant factor`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    "The unweighted expanded-row value is an implementation cross-check, not the H04 estimand. All quantities are point estimates without bootstrap intervals."
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.2)
```

The marginal fixed-effect R² has no unique term decomposition. A
hierarchy-respecting Shapley value function refits these five weighted models:

```r
geo_medi_1h ~ 1 + (1 | participant)
geo_medi_1h ~ site + (1 | participant)
geo_medi_1h ~ activity_named + (1 | participant)
geo_medi_1h ~ site + activity_named + (1 | participant)
geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + (1 | participant)
```

Site and activity are averaged over both admissible entry orders. Their
interaction enters only after both main effects. The resulting allocation is
invariant to the factor reference levels.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-participant-r2-shapley
#| tbl-cap: "Hierarchy-respecting allocation of the fractionally weighted marginal R²."

participant_random_intercept_shapley |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Component = .data$component,
    `R² component` = .data$marginal_r_squared_component,
    `Share of marginal R², %` =
      .data$share_of_full_marginal_r_squared_percent,
    `Efficiency error` = .data$shapley_efficiency_error
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `R² component`, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Share of marginal R², %`, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_scientific(columns = `Efficiency error`, decimals = 1) |>
  h04_gt(10.2)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-participant-r2-checks
#| tbl-cap: "Numerical checks for the ten nested mixed-model fits."

participant_random_intercept_models |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Model = .data$model_id,
    Formula = .data$formula,
    `Marginal R²` = .data$marginal_r_squared,
    `Conditional R²` = .data$conditional_r_squared,
    Converged = if_else(.data$converged, "Yes", "No"),
    Warnings = .data$warning_count,
    `Positive-definite Hessian` = if_else(
      .data$positive_definite_hessian,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    ),
    Singular = if_else(.data$singular, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(`Marginal R²`, `Conditional R²`), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Warnings) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Model ~ gt::pct(9),
    Formula ~ gt::pct(43),
    everything() ~ gt::pct(8)
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.0)
```

All ten nested fits converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians,
and were non-singular. The participant-hour aggregated lag-one Pearson
residual correlations were 0.317 near eye and 0.301 at chest. Observed zero
fractions were 0.294 and 0.301, compared with model-implied fractions of 0.410
and 0.429. This remains a descriptive point decomposition. It has no random
activity slopes, participant-day intercept, residual correlation structure,
or uncertainty intervals, and it does not replace the accepted population-mean
inference.

The exact [summary](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_participant_random_intercept_summary.csv),
[allocation](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_participant_random_intercept_marginal_r2_shapley.csv),
[diagnostics](../../../artifacts/08_diagnostics/H04/H04_participant_random_intercept_diagnostics.csv),
and [nested-model checks](../../../artifacts/08_diagnostics/H04/H04_participant_random_intercept_shapley_models.csv)
are stored with the fitted-model archive and a dedicated environment and
checksum manifest.

## Model checks, influence, and sensitivities

### Convergence, rank, covariance, and residual structure

Weighted long-row residual contributions are combined back to one value per
original hour before the residual-shape, calibration, zero-mass, and serial
dependence summaries are formed. Concurrent memberships are therefore not
treated as separate model-check observations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-primary-diagnostics
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded model checks for the additive primary and complementary GLMs."

main_diagnostics <- model_diagnostics |>
  filter(.data$scenario_id == "primary_dataset") |>
  mutate(
    placement = factor(
      .data$placement,
      levels = c("Near-eye", "Chest")
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(.data$placement)
overall_assessment <- diagnostic_assessments |>
  filter(.data$diagnostic == "Overall primary mean-model assessment") |>
  select("placement", "assessment")

main_diagnostics |>
  left_join(overall_assessment, by = "placement", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  transmute(
    Placement = as.character(.data$placement),
    Converged = if_else(.data$converged, "Yes", "No"),
    `Design rank` = paste0(.data$design_rank, "/", .data$design_columns),
    `Robust covariance positive definite` = if_else(
      .data$covariance_positive_definite,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    ),
    Dispersion = .data$dispersion,
    `Hour residual SD` = .data$hour_pearson_sd,
    `Residual lag 1` = .data$hour_residual_lag1_correlation,
    `Maximum cluster score share` =
      .data$maximum_cluster_score_share,
    `Maximum cluster leverage share` =
      .data$maximum_cluster_leverage_share,
    Assessment = tolower(.data$assessment)
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(Dispersion, `Hour residual SD`),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Residual lag 1`,
      `Maximum cluster score share`,
      `Maximum cluster leverage share`
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.8)
```

Both additive models converged without warnings, were full rank, and retained
finite positive-definite participant-clustered covariance. Large dispersion,
fitted-value-dependent spread, and residual lag-one correlations of 0.445 and
0.498 remain visible. The mean models are therefore acceptable with
limitation, not calibrated generative models.

### Deterministic influence checks

Every site was removed once within each placement. The five participants with
the largest cluster-score contribution were also removed once within each
placement. The model family, formula, weight definition, contrast direction,
and site-average estimation rule were preserved.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-influence
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded deterministic deletion-refit plan and primary-decision stability."

influence_summary <- influence_registry |>
  count(.data$placement, .data$deletion_type, name = "refits") |>
  left_join(
    influence_refits |>
      distinct(
        .data$placement,
        .data$deletion_type,
        .data$deletion_id,
        .data$primary_decision_changed
      ) |>
      group_by(.data$placement, .data$deletion_type) |>
      summarise(
        `Decision changes` = sum(.data$primary_decision_changed),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("placement", "deletion_type"),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Deletion unit` = recode(
      .data$deletion_type,
      site = "Site",
      participant = "High-score participant"
    ),
    Refits = .data$refits,
    `Primary-decision changes` = .data$`Decision changes`
  )

influence_summary |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(Refits, `Primary-decision changes`)) |>
  h04_gt()
```

None of the 27 deletion refits changed the five-category omnibus decision.
Category-ratio changes and intervals remain in the recorded influence table.

### Sensitivity analyses

The predefined branches change one aspect of the frame, weight, working
variance, or placement while preserving the category estimand whenever that
is possible. Exactly-one-category hours remove concurrent memberships.
Retaining co-selected Other deliberately reverses the primary specificity
rule. Excluding Other-only hours removes that varied display-only category,
which is not a coherent scientific category.
Unweighted long rows change the estimand by allowing multi-select hours to
contribute more than one total unit. The placement-matched branch uses the
same participants and participant-hours at the near-eye and chest sensor
positions, then fits each position separately; it is not an equivalence or
direct sensor-effect test. The remaining branches use the gap-timing-unaware
dataset, change the working power to 1.30 or 1.80, or use the complementary
chest position.

The additional Mundlak-style branch retains the accepted long rows and $1/k$
weights. For every participant it calculates the weighted share of retained
hours assigned to each of the five non-reference categories, then adds those
five participant-level proportions to the additive site-plus-activity mean
model. The current activity coefficients quantify category contrasts adjusted
for usual participant composition. A between-participant coefficient is
reported as the ratio for a 10 percentage-point higher usual category share,
which corresponds to a lower At home share while the other shares are held
fixed. Other remains unrestricted and display-only.

The **gap-timing-unaware dataset** still requires at least 50% valid minutes
per hour and at least 80% valid hours per day, but the timing of the remaining
missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific
adjustment. At this first explanation only, the primary dataset could be
interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset; hereafter it is called
the primary dataset.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-sensitivity-samples
#| tbl-cap: "Exact fitted samples for the predefined H04 sensitivity branches."

scenario_labels <- c(
  exactly_one_category = "Exactly one category",
  retain_coselected_other = "Retain co-selected Other",
  exclude_other_only = "Exclude Other-only hours",
  unweighted_long_rows = "Unweighted long rows",
  gap_timing_unaware = "Gap-timing-unaware dataset",
  paired_common_sample = "Placement-matched common sample",
  working_power_1_30 = "Quasi-Tweedie working power 1.30",
  working_power_1_80 = "Quasi-Tweedie working power 1.80",
  mundlak_within_between = "Within/between participant"
)

frame_index |>
  filter(.data$scenario_id %in% names(scenario_labels)) |>
  transmute(
    Sensitivity = unname(scenario_labels[.data$scenario_id]),
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    `Unique hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Long rows` = .data$long_rows,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    `Working power` = .data$working_power
  ) |>
  arrange(
    match(.data$Sensitivity, unname(scenario_labels)),
    factor(.data$Placement, levels = c("Near-eye", "Chest"))
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Sensitivity") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(
      Participants,
      `Participant-days`,
      `Unique hours`,
      `Long rows`
    ),
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = `Effective weighted hours`,
    decimals = 1,
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Working power`, decimals = 2) |>
  h04_gt(9.5)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-sensitivity-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded four-restriction five-category omnibus tests across sensitivity branches."

sensitivity_tests |>
  filter(.data$decision_role == "PRIMARY") |>
  mutate(Sensitivity = unname(scenario_labels[.data$scenario_id])) |>
  transmute(
    Sensitivity = .data$Sensitivity,

  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Sensitivity") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Wald F`, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Raw p`) |>
  h04_gt(9.8)
```

Every sensitivity omnibus was estimable and raw $p<0.001$. The recorded
[category-level sensitivity
comparison](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_sensitivity_comparison.csv)
contains the ratios, 95% intervals, relative changes, direction checks, and
whether the primary ratio lies inside each sensitivity interval.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-mundlak-support
#| tbl-cap: "Participant support for the H04 within/between sensitivity."

mundlak_support |>
  filter(.data$activity_code != "other") |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Activity = recode(
      .data$activity_code,
      working_indoor = "Office/home working",
      outdoors = "Outdoors",
      road_vehicle = "Vehicle/public transport",
      sleeping = "Sleeping"
    ),
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `With category` = .data$participants_with_category,
    `With category and At home` =
      .data$participants_with_category_and_home,
    `Mean category share, %` = 100 * .data$mean_activity_share,
    `Median category share, %` = 100 * .data$median_activity_share,
    `Maximum category share, %` = 100 * .data$maximum_activity_share
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Activity = factor(
      .data$Activity,
      levels = c(
        "Office/home working",
        "Outdoors",
        "Vehicle/public transport",
        "Sleeping"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(
    factor(.data$Placement, levels = c("Near-eye", "Chest")),
    .data$Activity
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(Participants, `With category`, `With category and At home`)
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = ends_with("share, %"),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.5)
```

Every participant contributed At home hours. Direct within-participant support
for the category-versus-home contrast ranged from 111 participants for
near-eye vehicle or public-transport activity to all 150 chest participants
for Sleeping. Both Mundlak fits converged, were full rank (19/19 near eye and
18/18 at chest), and had finite positive-definite participant-clustered
covariance. The covariance condition numbers were 7,048 and 4,301, below the
predefined $10^{10}$ threshold.

The four-restriction within-participant category tests were $F(4,125)=67.17$,
raw $p<0.001$, near eye and $F(4,149)=77.86$, raw $p<0.001$, at chest. All four
named ratios retained their direction, changed by at most 16.8%, and contained
the primary ratio within the sensitivity interval. The four named
between-participant composition terms were jointly associated near eye,
$F(4,125)=3.81$, raw $p=0.006$, but not clearly at chest, $F(4,149)=2.34$, raw
$p=0.058$. The exact [within-participant comparison](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_sensitivity_comparison.csv),
[between-participant estimates](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_mundlak_between_participant_estimands.csv),
and [between-participant omnibus tests](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H04/H04_mundlak_between_participant_omnibus.csv)
retain all ratios, 95% CIs, p-values, and FDR values.

## Exploratory nonlinear time-of-day context

### Weighted activity GAMs

The exploratory nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is
separate from the primary population-mean inference. It allows the association
with clock time to bend across the day, using the same long rows and exact
$1/k$ weights with this exact formula:

```r
geo_medi_1h ~
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, activity, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
```

The global time smooth uses a cyclic cubic basis and joins across midnight.
The activity and site sum-to-zero deviations use the approved thin-plate
marginal basis and are not cyclic, so their fitted endpoints may separate at
midnight. Participant-specific smooths and participant-day random intercepts
remain in the fit. Activity-specific residual runs ensure that concurrent
memberships at one timestamp never become lag neighbours.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-basis
#| tbl-cap: "Constructed smooth classes and midnight continuity."

temporal_basis |>
  transmute(
    Component = recode(
      .data$component,
      `global time` = "Global time",
      `activity deviation` = "Activity deviation",
      `site deviation` = "Site deviation"
    ),
    `Constructed class` = .data$constructed_class,
    `Marginal basis` = .data$marginal_basis,
    `Cyclic across midnight` = if_else(.data$cyclic, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  h04_gt()
```

`mgcv::bam()` used a fixed-power Tweedie mean with log link, fREML, discrete
computation, one R thread, and cyclic knots at 0 and 24 hours. A preliminary
zero-correlation fit supplied the boundary-aware lag-one residual correlation;
the final model used that value as its working AR(1) parameter.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-models
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded final exploratory time-of-day model settings and model checks."

temporal_activity <- temporal_comparison |>
  filter(.data$formula_id == "temporal_activity_long") |>
  arrange(match(.data$placement, c("Near-eye", "Chest")))

temporal_activity |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Long rows` = .data$observations_long_rows,
    `Unique participant-hours` = .data$unique_participant_hours,
    `Effective weighted hours` = .data$effective_weighted_hours,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Sites = .data$sites,
    Activities = .data$activities,
    `AR(1) rho` = .data$rho,
    `Adjusted R²` = .data$adjusted_r_squared,
    `Deviance explained` = .data$deviance_explained,
    `Residual lag 1` = .data$standardized_residual_lag1,
    Converged = if_else(.data$converged, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(
    columns = c(
      `Long rows`,
      `Unique participant-hours`,
      Participants,
      `Participant-days`,
      Sites,
      Activities
    ),
    sep_mark = ","
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Effective weighted hours`,
      `AR(1) rho`,
      `Adjusted R²`,
      `Deviance explained`,
      `Residual lag 1`
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  h04_gt(9.2)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded descriptive comparison of time-of-day models with and without activity deviations."

temporal_comparison_display <- temporal_comparison |>
  select(
    "placement",
    "formula_id",
    "aic",
    "deviance_explained"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = "formula_id",
    values_from = c("aic", "deviance_explained")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `AIC improvement with activity` =
      .data$aic_temporal_no_activity -
      .data$aic_temporal_activity_long,
    `Deviance explained with activity` =
      .data$deviance_explained_temporal_activity_long,
    `Deviance explained without activity` =
      .data$deviance_explained_temporal_no_activity
  )

temporal_comparison_display |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `AIC improvement with activity`, decimals = 0) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(
    columns = c(
      `Deviance explained with activity`,
      `Deviance explained without activity`
    ),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    "This is descriptive contextual evidence, not a second primary activity test or a likelihood-ratio decision."
  ) |>
  h04_gt()
```

Activity deviations improved AIC by 3,215 near eye and 4,984 at chest, while
deviance explained increased from 81.8% to 84.8% and from 79.5% to 83.2%.
Both fits are retained as exploratory context.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-retention
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded construction and adequacy evidence for the exploratory activity models."

temporal_retention |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    `Convergence checks` = if_else(.data$convergence_pass, "Pass", "Fail"),
    `Weight and run checks` = if_else(
      .data$run_boundary_and_weight_pass,
      "Pass",
      "Fail"
    ),
    `Minimum finite k-index` = .data$minimum_finite_k_index,
    `Residual lag 1` = .data$residual_lag1,
    `Locally sparse clock/activity cells` =
      .data$locally_sparse_clock_activity_cells,
    `Maximum activity endpoint ratio` =
      .data$maximum_activity_endpoint_ratio,
    `Maximum site endpoint ratio` = .data$maximum_site_endpoint_ratio,
    Assessment = tolower(.data$assessment)
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(`Minimum finite k-index`, `Residual lag 1`),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      `Maximum activity endpoint ratio`,
      `Maximum site endpoint ratio`
    ),
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = `Locally sparse clock/activity cells`) |>
  h04_gt(9.8)
```

The models converged at full coefficient rank with positive smoothing
Hessians. Residual dependence, 41 near-eye and 40 chest locally sparse
clock/activity cells, the working zero-mass mismatch, and non-cyclic
activity/site endpoints remain explicit limitations.

### Population curves and uncertainty

Displayed time/activity curves set participant and participant-day
contributions to zero, evaluate every site observed at that sensor position,
average those design rows equally on the fitted log-mean scale, and
back-transform once to melEDI in lux. Their ribbons are model-based pointwise
95% CIs from the fitted coefficient covariance. A pointwise interval applies
to one displayed clock time rather than to the entire curve simultaneously.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-uncertainty
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded uncertainty construction for the exploratory temporal curves."

temporal_uncertainty |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Implementation = .data$implementation,
    `Interval type` = .data$interval_type,
    `Covariance source` = .data$covariance_source,
    `Critical value` = .data$interval_critical_value,
    `Resampling replicates` = .data$resampling_replicates,
    `Simultaneous band` = if_else(.data$simultaneous_band, "Yes", "No"),
    `Curve-wide inference` = if_else(
      .data$curve_wide_inference,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    )
  ) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Critical value`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = `Resampling replicates`) |>
  h04_gt(9.8)
```

No bootstrap or simulation enters these curves. The intervals are not
simultaneous bands, and no time-specific significant period or curve-wide
inference is reported.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-temporal-performance
#| tbl-cap: "Stored participant-balanced temporal-model performance and fitted-variance allocation."

temporal_performance <- temporal_r_squared |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement,
    Quantity = "Participant-balanced raw-scale R²",
    Value = .data$r_squared
  ) |>
  bind_rows(
    temporal_allocation |>
      transmute(
        Placement = .data$placement,
        Quantity = recode(
          .data$group,
          global_time = "Global time allocated share",
          activity_deviations = "Activity-deviation allocated share",
          site_deviations = "Site-deviation allocated share",
          participant_curves = "Participant-curve allocated share",
          participant_day_shifts = "Participant-day-shift allocated share"
        ),
        Value = .data$shapley_share
      )
  )

temporal_performance |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      .data$Placement,
      levels = c("Near-eye", "Chest")
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(.data$Placement, .data$Quantity) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = Value, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    "The R² is on the raw melEDI scale with site-average and participant balance and 1/k within-hour weights. Allocated shares partition fitted natural-log predictor variance and are point summaries without uncertainty intervals."
  ) |>
  h04_gt()
```

The hierarchy-respecting Shapley allocation distributes shared fitted-model
information across the temporal components rather than counting overlapping
contributions more than once. It reports point estimates without uncertainty
intervals. The remaining positive lag-one residual correlations mean that
neighbouring hourly residuals are still related after the working AR(1)
correction.

The [near-eye](../../../artifacts/10_figures/H04/H04_temporal_near_eye.png)
and [chest](../../../artifacts/10_figures/H04/H04_temporal_chest.png) results
figures show the fitted activity curves, activity-to-global ratios, and
effective weighted support. Their exact curve and support values are stored
under `artifacts/11_source_data/H04/`.

## Technical provenance and reproduction

### Render-time computation boundary

Rendering this page recalculates only current file identities and lightweight
descriptive summaries from recorded, checksummed H04 model frames and source
tables. It does not fit or refit a model, calculate a model prediction,
re-estimate residual dependence, rerun a deletion analysis, bootstrap,
simulate data, or recalculate a variance allocation. Model estimates, 95%
CIs, tests, model checks, sensitivities, and exploratory smooths are read from
their recorded files.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-boundary
#| tbl-cap: "Calculations performed when this page is rendered."

tibble::tribble(
  ~Category, ~Calculated_on_render, ~Explanation,
  "File identity and schema", "Yes", "Checks recorded SHA-256 identities, required columns, recorded-frame dimensions, and source-table structure.",
  "Descriptive support", "Yes", "Summarises stored sample flow, fractional weights, categories, sites, local hours, participant-days, and exact zeros.",
  "Model construction and estimation", "No", "Reads formula records, fitted-model archives, estimates, intervals, and robust tests.",
  "Model checks and sensitivities", "No", "Reads recorded model checks, deletion refits, fit summaries, and sensitivity outputs.",
  "Preparation figures", "Display only", "Draws four descriptive figures from linked exact source-data CSV files."
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(Calculated_on_render = "Calculated on render") |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Category ~ gt::pct(24),
    Calculated_on_render ~ gt::pct(18),
    Explanation ~ gt::pct(58)
  ) |>
  h04_gt()
```

### Environment identity

The scientific analysis and this companion use R 4.6.1 and the synchronized
project library. The stored environment tables record the primary GLM,
mixed-model, and reporting packages; the same library supplies `mgcv` and
`gratia` for the exploratory temporal analysis.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h04-prep-environment
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded R and consequential package versions."

environment_display <- software_environment |>
  filter(.data$component %in% c(
    "R",
    "R package: dplyr",
    "R package: readr",
    "R package: statmod",
    "R package: sandwich",
    "R package: ggplot2",
    "R package: gt"
  )) |>
  bind_rows(
    participant_random_intercept_environment |>
      filter(.data$component %in% c(
        "glmmTMB", "lme4", "performance", "insight"
      )) |>
      transmute(
        component = paste0("R package: ", .data$component),
        version = .data$version
      ),
    tibble(
      component = c(
        "R package: mgcv",
        "R package: gratia",
        "Quarto CLI",
        "renv.lock SHA-256 prefix"
      ),
      version = c(
        as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")),
        as.character(packageVersion("gratia")),
        Sys.getenv("QUARTO_VERSION", unset = "1.9.37"),
        substr(artifact_sha256(file.path(root, "renv.lock")), 1L, 16L)
      )
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(Component = .data$component, Version = .data$version)

environment_display |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(Component ~ gt::pct(68), Version ~ gt::pct(32)) |>
  h04_gt()
```

### Examination order

For a bounded verification that does not recompute a model:

1. verify the five scientific input identities in
   `artifacts/06_model_data/H04/H04_input_audit.csv`;
2. inspect `H04_model_frames.rds`, `H04_model_frame_index.csv`, and the seven
   preparation source-data CSVs for the exact long rows, unique hours, $k$,
   weights, and support;
3. compare formulas and transformation rules with `h04_contract.R`,
   `h04_stage1_support.R`, `h04_data.R`, and `h04_modeling.R`;
4. trace each reported number to `artifacts/09_tables/H04/` and each
   model-check statement to `artifacts/08_diagnostics/H04/`;
5. rebuild displays only from their paired CSVs in
   `artifacts/11_source_data/H04/`; and
6. verify the final identities in
   `H04_preparation_report_manifest.csv`.

The lightweight preparation inputs are regenerated with:

```bash
Rscript --vanilla scripts/hypotheses/H04/build_h04_preparation_artifacts.R
```

The [H04 results report](../../../notebooks/hypotheses/H04.qmd) is the
appropriate page for scientific interpretation. This companion records how
that report was constructed and how its evidence can be checked.
